lifted_by: json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode four times from the byte after the 'cells' array's opening bracket; the span is the bytes those four elements occupy, separators and whitespace included, with no trailing comma
source: src/tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json at contract_version 22 (origin/master 3ec01f26); re-spanned at contract_version 24 (#460) and again at 31 (tessera#538), without re-measuring any surviving cell; re-spanned at 32 (tessera#506 leg 2) when the E2M1_K2 dense cells' rungs_q256 widened to the full trellis domain, again without re-measuring — the two E4M3 routed cells in the span are untouched
what: The v22 sm_121 cells that SURVIVE at contract_version 32, recorded as a digest. Contract v22 published ten; v31 withdrew six of them (tessera#538) and the four below are what is left, still the first four elements of lane_eligibility.cells.
why_not_the_bytes: A copy of the array would repeat the runtime image pin, and tests/test_runtime_image_pin.py refuses a second copy of that digest in any file that acts. A hash pins the same bytes without holding the pin.
withdrawn_why: They attested the dense window-GEMV lane. Commit 1b767a207 left fp8_route.apply and bf16_route.apply making one launch each -- tessera::window_gemm_dense/native_window_gemm -- so the build could no longer make the arithmetic these cells published, and every receipt behind them predates that commit. A withdrawal is neither an addition nor a re-measurement, so it is named here rather than absorbed into a new digest.
